# Every generated file, explained

The installer writes **real files** into your existing project and prints their paths. This example is for a TypeScript Next.js application with `src/app/`.

<FileTree title="Files created in a TypeScript src/app project" items={[{
  name:"my-docs",kind:"folder",children:[
    {name:"nextguide.config.json",kind:"json"},
    {name:"content",kind:"folder",children:[{name:"docs",kind:"folder",children:[{name:"_meta.json",kind:"json"},{name:"index.mdx",kind:"code"},{name:"getting-started.mdx",kind:"code"}]}]},
    {name:"src",kind:"folder",children:[
      {name:"lib",kind:"folder",children:[{name:"nextguide.ts",kind:"code"}]},
      {name:"styles",kind:"folder",children:[{name:"nextguide.css",kind:"file"}]},
      {name:"app",kind:"folder",children:[{name:"docs",kind:"folder",children:[{name:"layout.tsx",kind:"code"},{name:"[[...slug]]",kind:"folder",children:[{name:"page.tsx",kind:"code"}]}]}]}
    ]}
  ]
}]} />

## What each file does

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `nextguide.config.json` | Site title, description, content folder and active mode |
| `content/docs/index.mdx` | Your `/docs` homepage; editable Markdown + JSX |
| `content/docs/getting-started.mdx` | A second page so you can test navigation immediately |
| `content/docs/_meta.json` | Sidebar order and labels (one entry per page) |
| `src/lib/nextguide.ts` | Creates the MDX source, enables plugins and exposes the site configuration |
| `src/app/docs/layout.tsx` | Renders your documentation header and sidebar and imports CSS |
| `src/app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx` | Turns an MDX filename into `/docs/...` routes and static paths |
| `src/styles/nextguide.css` | Editable, responsive starter design scoped under `ng-starter` |

### App Router vs Pages Router

For `app/` without `src/`, NextGuide uses `app/docs/...`, `lib/nextguide.ts`, and `styles/nextguide.css` instead. JavaScript projects receive `.jsx` and `.js` files.

For the **Pages Router**, the CLI creates `pages/docs/[[...slug]].tsx` (or the `src/pages` equivalent) using `getStaticPaths` and `getStaticProps`. It creates `pages/_app.tsx` if missing, or adds only the required CSS imports to your existing `_app` without discarding the rest of your code.

## The actual generated code

These examples are taken directly from the template emitted by `nextguide init`, not pseudocode. They are editable after generation.

### Site configuration

`nextguide.config.json`

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "mode": "developer",
  "contentDir": "content/docs",
  "site": {
    "name": "My Documentation",
    "description": "Documentation built with NextGuide"
  }
}
```

### Navigation order

`content/docs/_meta.json`

```json
[
  {
    "slug": "index",
    "title": "Introduction"
  },
  {
    "slug": "getting-started",
    "title": "Getting started"
  }
]
```

### MDX source

`src/lib/nextguide.ts`

```ts
// Generated by NextGuide CLI. Edit freely; NextGuide never overwrites these files.
import { createDocs } from "nextguide/mdx"
import { remarkGfm, rehypeSlug } from "nextguide/mdx/plugins"
import config from "../../nextguide.config.json"

export const site = config.site
export const docs = createDocs({
  contentDir: config.contentDir,
  remarkPlugins: [remarkGfm],
  rehypePlugins: [rehypeSlug],
})
```

### Header and sidebar

`src/app/docs/layout.tsx`

```tsx
// Generated by NextGuide CLI. Edit freely; NextGuide never overwrites these files.
import Link from "next/link"
import type { ReactNode } from "react"
import { docs, site } from "../../lib/nextguide"
import "nextguide/styles.css"
import "../../styles/nextguide.css"

type LinkItem = { title: string; href: string; nav: boolean; items: LinkItem[] }
function renderNavigation(items: LinkItem[]) {
  return items.filter((item) => item.nav).map((item) => (
    <li key={item.href}>
      <Link href={"/docs" + (item.href === "/" ? "" : item.href)}>{item.title}</Link>
      {item.items.length ? <ul>{renderNavigation(item.items)}</ul> : null}
    </li>
  ))
}

export default async function DocumentationLayout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const navigation = await docs.getNavigation()
  return (
    <div className="ng-starter">
      <header className="ng-starter-header"><Link href="/docs">{site.name}</Link><span>Documentation</span></header>
      <div className="ng-starter-body">
        <aside className="ng-starter-sidebar" aria-label="Documentation navigation">
          <nav><ul>{renderNavigation(navigation)}</ul></nav>
        </aside>
        <main className="ng-starter-main">{children}</main>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Routing and MDX rendering

`src/app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx`

```tsx
// Generated by NextGuide CLI. Edit freely; NextGuide never overwrites these files.
import { notFound } from "next/navigation"
import { isMdxNotFound } from "nextguide/mdx"
import { docs } from "../../../lib/nextguide"

export const dynamicParams = false

export async function generateStaticParams() {
  const paths = await docs.getPagePaths()
  return paths.map((path) => ({ slug: path.split("/").filter(Boolean) }))
}

export default async function DocumentationPage({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug?: string[] }> }) {
  const slug = ((await params).slug ?? []).join("/")
  try {
    const { MDX, frontmatter } = await docs.parse({ slug })
    return (
      <article className="ng-starter-prose">
        <h1>{String(frontmatter.title ?? "Documentation")}</h1>
        {frontmatter.description ? <p className="ng-starter-description">{String(frontmatter.description)}</p> : null}
        {MDX}
      </article>
    )
  } catch (error) {
    if (isMdxNotFound(error)) notFound()
    throw error
  }
}
```

## Files added when you create another page

After running the initializer, you can use `bunx nextguide page add guides/setup` to generate new MDX pages. The command uses the `contentDir` configured in `nextguide.config.json`.

For the example `guides/setup`, NextGuide creates `content/docs/guides/setup.mdx`, creates `content/docs/guides/_meta.json` if missing, and appends the `guides` section to the existing root `_meta.json`. An existing page is never replaced, and the sidebar settings already stored in metadata are preserved.

[Create your first page](/docs/getting-started/adding-pages).

## Overwrite protection

NextGuide checks the full proposed file list **before writing**. If one of the names already exists, the operation fails instead of replacing user code. Use `--dry-run` to see the paths first.

<CodeWindow title="Preview before writing" language="powershell" code="bunx nextguide init --developer --dry-run" />
